title: How to Check If Your Email Was in a Data Breach
html:
Two checks answer this in a few minutes. Search your email address on Have I Been Pwned to see which known breaches included it. Then run Google Password Checkup to see which of your saved passwords are exposed, weak or reused. If either shows a problem, change that password first, then turn on 2-Step Verification for the account.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026.

I ran both checks on 11 Oct 2026: the Have I Been Pwned check on my own email address in a private browser window, and the Checkup tab in Google Password Manager on my vivo V23 Pro (Android 14, Funtouch OS 14).

1. Check your email on Have I Been Pwned

Have I Been Pwned (haveibeenpwned.com) is a free site created by security researcher Troy Hunt in 2013, to help people see whether an online account of theirs has been caught up in a breach. Type your email address and it shows the breaches that included it. Its FAQ says the public search returns results for one address at a time, and that the site does not log searches or store the addresses you search. If you choose the "Notify me" service, it does store the address, along with the sign-up date and a verification token, so it can warn you about future breaches.

Read the result carefully. "Pwned" means your address was in the data from that breach. It does not mean someone has logged in to your account. The page lists what was exposed, such as email addresses, passwords or phone numbers. If passwords were included, assume that password is known.

2. Check your saved passwords with Google Password Checkup

On Android, open Chrome, tap More, then Settings, then Autofill and passwords, then Google Password Manager, then Checkup. You can also go to passwords.google.com/checkup/start. Google checks your saved passwords and labels them Exposed, Weak or Used in multiple accounts. Google explains that compromised combinations are unsafe because they have been published online, and recommends changing them as soon as you can.

Have I Been Pwned showed "Oh no, pwned!" with 1 data breach for my address. I am not naming the breach. The Checkup tab in Google Password Manager has three sections: compromised passwords ("You should change these now"), reused passwords ("Create unique passwords") and weak passwords ("Create strong passwords"). It also says how many sites and apps it checked. On my phone all three sections had passwords in them, so this check was worth doing.

3. If something shows up

  1. Change the exposed password on that site, and on any other site where you used the same one. Google warns that using the same password on several accounts puts you at greater risk.
  2. Turn on 2-Step Verification on the account. See our guide to two-factor authentication.
  3. Check your main email first. If your email account is exposed, every reset link goes there. Our Google account checklist covers Gmail.
  4. Expect phishing. After a breach, messages that mention the site can look more convincing. Learn what to check.

If you see sign-ins or one-time codes you did not ask for, read what an unrequested OTP means.

What to do next

  1. Search your main email address on Have I Been Pwned.
  2. Run Google Password Checkup and fix everything marked Exposed or Used in multiple accounts.
  3. Turn on 2-Step Verification for your email and bank accounts.
